2. Mark the centre point: Find the centre of your wall section and use a pencil to mark it lightly. Hang the middle print centred on this mark, then work outwards to position the left and right prints with an equal gap between each one — 5 to 8 cm is a good starting point.

I'd hang all three in a straight horizontal row above a bed or along a bedroom wall, with equal gaps between each print — around 5 to 8 cm works really well and keeps things looking intentional without being rigid. Hold a piece of paper up to the wall (or use masking tape to mark out the rough footprint of all three) — it sounds simple, but it really does help you picture it.

What are bedroom wall frames?

Bedroom wall frames are art prints displayed in a frame and hung on the wall to decorate a bedroom, adding colour, personality and a finished look to the space. They come in sets — like this set of 3 — or as single pieces, and are available in a range of sizes to suit everything from a small accent wall to a full feature wall above a bed. You can choose framed prints that arrive ready to hang straight away, or unframed prints if you prefer to use your own frames. At AboutWallArt, bedroom wall frames are available in multiple sizes, in Luster or Museum quality paper, and also as wrapped canvas prints — so you can find exactly the right look for your room.

How to Hang Bedroom Wall Frames in 5 Simple Steps

1. Choose your wall and measure up: Decide where you want to hang the prints — above the bed is the most popular spot. Measure the width of the space and divide by the number of prints (3) plus the gaps between them to work out where each print should sit.

2. Cut paper templates: Cut three pieces of paper or card to the size of your chosen prints. Tape them to the wall with masking tape so you can stand back and check the layout before making any holes.

3. Mark your hanging points: Once you're happy with the position, mark the top centre of each template lightly with a pencil. Measure down to find the hanging hook position on the back of each frame and mark those points on the wall.

4. Fix your hooks or picture nails: Use picture nails, adhesive strips or D-ring hooks depending on your wall type. For heavier framed prints, a proper picture nail into a wall plug gives the most secure hold.

5. Hang, level and step back: Hang each print, use a small spirit level to check they're straight, then adjust the gaps so they're even. Step back across the room to check the overall effect — small tweaks at this stage make a big difference to the finished look.

Choosing Your Bedroom Wall Frames Format: Which Option Is Right for You?

Unframed Print — The print is delivered on its own (Luster or Museum quality paper). Great if you already have frames you love or want to choose your own. Most affordable option. You will need to source and fit a frame yourself.

Framed Print — Arrives ready to hang straight out of the packaging — no extra shopping or hassle. Available in multiple sizes with a choice of Luster or Museum quality paper. Ideal if you want a neat, complete look without the effort of framing.

Wrapped Canvas — The artwork is printed directly onto canvas and stretched over a wooden frame, giving a contemporary, frameless look. Arrives ready to hang. No paper or glass — just the printed canvas. Perfect for a more relaxed, modern or boho bedroom style.

Paper Quality: Luster — A semi-gloss finish that brings out colours vibrantly with a slight sheen. Handles reflections better than high-gloss. A brilliant all-round choice for most bedrooms.

Paper Quality: Museum — A fine-art matte finish favoured for high-detail, painterly or illustrated artwork like this London set. No glare, rich depth of tone, and a premium feel. Ideal if you want the closest look to an original illustration.

What are bedroom framed pictures?

Bedroom framed pictures are art prints or illustrations sold ready to display in a bedroom, either unframed, in a frame, or wrapped on canvas — giving you a finished look on your walls without any extra effort. They come in a range of sizes to suit different wall spaces, from small bedside displays to large statement pieces above a headboard. The framed options in particular arrive ready to hang straight away, making them one of the easiest ways to personalise a bedroom. At AboutWallArt, our bedroom framed pictures are printed in the UK with fade-resistant inks so the colours stay fresh and vibrant for years.

How to Hang Bedroom Framed Pictures in 5 Simple Steps

1. Choose your wall space: Decide where you want to hang your prints — above the headboard is the most popular spot, but a chimney breast, an alcove, or the wall opposite the bed all work well too.

2. Pick your size: Hold a piece of paper or a magazine up to the wall to get a rough feel for scale. For a set of 3 above a double or king-size bed, medium to large prints usually give the best balance.

3. Plan the layout before you hang: Lay all three prints on the floor in front of the wall and decide on your spacing. A consistent gap of 5–10 cm between each print looks clean and intentional.

4. Mark your hanging points: Use a pencil and a spirit level to mark where each hook or nail will go. Getting this step right saves a lot of fiddling later.

5. Hang and step back: Put the prints up, step back to the doorway, and check the alignment from a distance — that's when small adjustments become obvious and easy to fix before you're done.

Choosing Your Print Option: What's the Difference?

Unframed Print — The art print on its own, ready for you to frame however you like. Great if you have a specific frame style in mind or want to match existing frames in your bedroom. Available in Luster or Museum quality paper.

Framed Print — The art print presented in a frame and ready to hang the moment it arrives — no extra trips to the shop needed. A brilliant time-saver. Available in Luster or Museum quality paper, in multiple sizes.

Wrapped Canvas — The artwork printed directly onto canvas and stretched over a wooden frame with the image continuing around the edges. A contemporary, frameless look that suits more modern bedroom styles. Available in multiple size options.

Luster Art Paper — A slightly satin finish that handles soft watercolour tones beautifully and reduces glare in rooms with natural light. A great all-round everyday choice.

Museum Quality Paper — The premium paper option, giving the sharpest detail, richest colour depth, and the finest reproduction of delicate linework and watercolour washes. Worth choosing if you want the very best result.
